title: Plan
description:
A logical plan: a directed acyclic graph of operator nodes connected by edges between their ports.

Every input and output port of every node has exactly one edge; fan-out and fan-in exist only through the routing operators `tee` and `merge`, and every path ends in an `emit` to a declared output or in a `drop`. Validation checks these rules and more; deserializing a plan checks only its shape.

A plan's nodes and edges are kept in the order they are written, and are hashed in that order. Producers of plans, such as lowering, emit them in a deterministic order.

# Normalized form

Serializing a plan writes its **normalized form**: members whose value is their default, such as an empty list of outputs or recipients and the native delivery policy, are left out. A plan read from its normalized form writes the same document back, and its [hash][Self::hash] is the RFC 8785 digest of that document. A document that writes a default explicitly reads as the same plan, and has the same hash, although its own digest differs.

ir_version.description: The IR version the plan is written in.

outputs.description: The declared outputs that `emit` nodes deliver to.

provenance.description:
Where the plan as a whole came from.

Plan-level provenance describes the plan's origin, not what it does, so it is not part of the plan's [hash][Self::hash].

resources.description:
The resources the plan's outputs deliver through: each delivery host's settings, and every recipient.

Resources are plan parameters, so a change of any of them is a new plan, with a new hash. Only the host's own lowering declares them: an artifact cannot.

ArtifactRevision.description: One revision of an approved artifact.

revision.description: The artifact's revision number. Revisions strictly increase.

BoundedDelivery.description:
A recipient's delivery within bounds tighter than its host's native ones.

A dual-ship destination added for an experiment should not take the primary's memory, should not fill the disk, and may not deserve the whole drain deadline of retries when it is removed: these knobs cover that.

on_retire.description: What the recipient does with its queued work when it retires.

queue_bytes.description: The bound of the recipient's in-memory retry queue, in bytes, at most the native configured bound; `None` keeps the native bound.

spill.description: Whether the recipient's queue spills to disk.

Closure.description:
What an output or recipient does with queued work when it closes, at process shutdown or when it retires.

Serialized as its name, such as `"attempt"`.

oneOf.description: Native shutdown: in-flight requests finish within the shutdown timeout, and queued work is persisted where configured, and otherwise dropped. A retiring generation's batches finish in the shared encoder streams, which do not close, so a live update loses nothing beyond what a native shutdown would.
Queued work is attempted until the drain deadline, then closed as at native shutdown.
Queued work is persisted where disk storage is configured, without further attempts, and otherwise dropped.
Queued work is dropped and counted.

DeliveryPolicy.description:
What an output or recipient does when it is full, and when it closes.

The slot is open to resources artifacts for the recipients they declare, mapping onto native mechanisms only: a [`Bounded`][Self::Bounded] policy can shrink a recipient's queue, forbid spilling it to disk, and choose what happens to its queued work when it retires. Nothing can raise a native bound. Outputs keep the native policy.

Serialized as `"native"`, or as `{"bounded": {...}}` with the members of [`BoundedDelivery`].

oneOf.description:
The native behavior.

An output waits for its downstream to accept more. A recipient queues requests in a byte-bounded retry queue that evicts the oldest entries, or spills them to disk where configured, and sends fresh requests before retries. On close, in-flight requests finish within the shutdown timeout, and queued work is persisted where configured and otherwise dropped.
Native mechanisms within tighter bounds, for a recipient a resources artifact declares.

Edge.description: An edge from one node's output port to another node's input port.

from.description: The output port the edge leaves.

to.description: The input port the edge enters.

HostBinding.description: A delivery host's shared settings: its client profile (proxies, TLS, timeouts, HTTP protocol), and its retry and concurrency settings, as the host's schema declares them.

Kind.description:
The kind of a metric.

Each kind corresponds to one variant of [`MetricValues`]. A rate's interval is part of its values, not of its kind: predicates and port types never distinguish rates by interval.

oneOf.description: A sum of deltas.
A total change over an interval.
A latest value.
A set of distinct members.
A collection of samples, aggregated on the client side.
A sketch of samples, mergeable on the server side.

KindSet.description: A set of metric kinds: `"all"`, or a list of distinct kinds.

NativeComponentId.description: The identifier of a native component.

Node.description:
One operator node.

A node's ports follow from its operator and parameters: for example, a `split` has the output ports `true` and `false`, and a `tee` has as many numbered output ports as its parameters say.

id.description: The node's identifier, stable across generations.

op.description: The registered operator the node runs.

NodeId.description: A node ID: an identifier, the node's name.

OutputBinding.description:
An output's resolved binding: where and how the records emitted to it are encoded and delivered.

An output with a binding runs as a **lease** in the encode host of its delivery host: one encoder stream with the binding's parameters. A binding change creates a new lease, and the old one drains once no generation uses it.

encoder.description: The encoder's parameters, as the host's schema declares them: protocol variants, compression, payload limits, and flush timeout, for example.

host.description: The delivery host the output delivers through.

selector.description: What the output's declaration says it delivers to, which its fingerprint covers.

telemetry.description: The component identifier the output's encoder telemetry reports under.

OutputDecl.description: A declared output: a destination that `emit` nodes deliver to, bound to one encoder stream and its recipients.

accepts.description: The type of the records the output accepts.

binding.description: The output's resolved binding to a delivery host, or `None` for a fixed destination, such as an internal tap, which runs in a component of its own.

delivery.description: What the output does when it cannot keep up or when it closes. Defaults to the native policy.

recipients.description:
The physical recipients the output delivers to, sorted and without repeats. Outputs that share a recipient feed the same delivery queue.

An output without recipients, such as an internal tap, delivers to no endpoint. A bound output's recipients are those the plan's [resources](Plan::resources) declare on its delivery host.

Params.description: Operator parameters, keyed by parameter name. Each operator's parameter schema defines their types.

PayloadClasses.description:
Which payloads a recipient receives when a payload does not name its recipients itself.

Metrics payloads from leases name their recipients, so classes decide where every other payload goes: logs, events, service checks, traces, and APM statistics, for example.

oneOf.description: Metrics only: a recipient that only metrics are routed to, such as the Cluster Agent or a metrics override.
Every class of payload, as an additional endpoint natively receives.

PlanHash.description: A SHA-256 digest: `sha256:` followed by 64 lowercase hexadecimal digits.

PlanProvenance.description: Where a plan as a whole came from.

artifact.description: The artifact revision the plan runs: every node of the plan but its sources is the artifact's. A plan without one is the default program.

config_change.description: The number of the configuration change the plan was lowered from, counted per process.

native_components.description:
Which native component each node of a lowered default program does the work of, as lowering writes it.

This describes native configuration's topology, for the layout the host builds at boot from its default program: R1's cost model prices native components, not nodes, and a host may size a region's input by the native components it replaces. It decides nothing else: not what a node may do, not who answers for its loss, and not what a later generation reuses. Composition does not carry it, since a composed plan is never a boot plan. A node it does not list is a component of its own.

PortType.description: The type of the records a port carries: their kinds and their timestamp form.

kinds.description: The kinds of metric the port carries.

timestamps.description: Which of the port's points carry a timestamp.

RecipientDecl.description:
One recipient of a delivery host: one endpoint, with its credential, its queue, and its persisted directory.

Recipients are shared by every output whose binding names them: outputs that share a recipient feed the same delivery queue.

classes.description: Which payloads the recipient receives when a payload does not name its recipients.

credential.description: A reference to the credential the recipient sends with: never the credential's value.

delivery.description: The recipient's delivery policy: its only knobs beyond its host's settings. Defaults to the native policy.

endpoint.description: The endpoint, as configured for a native recipient, or in canonical form for a declared one.

host.description: The delivery host it belongs to.

protocol.description: The recipient's protocol, as the host's schema declares it: which protocol variants it accepts, and how its requests are formed, for example.

Resources.description:
The resources of a plan: the settings of each delivery host, and every recipient the plan names.

Serialized as the plan member `resources`, left out when empty.

hosts.description: The shared settings of each delivery host, at most one per host.

recipients.description: Every recipient the plan's outputs, and the native recipient sets of its delivery hosts, name, at most one per recipient ID.

Selector.description:
What an output's declaration says it delivers to.

An output's fingerprint covers its selector, not its resolved recipients: a role delivers to whatever native configuration resolves for it, so its recipients can change without changing its fingerprint, while an explicit recipient list is part of the declaration.

Serialized as an object with one member: `{"role": "main"}`, `{"group": "sha256:<hex>"}`, or `{"recipients": [<recipient ID>, ...]}`.

oneOf.description: A role of the delivery host, such as `main`, `multi_region_failover`, or `autoscaling_failover`.
A routing group, by its key.
Exactly these recipients, sorted and without duplicates: an **implied output**, which the host adds for the recipients a program's `emit`s address when no other output delivers to exactly them.

Spill.description: Whether a recipient's queue spills to disk.

oneOf.description: As configured for the host: to disk where disk storage is configured.
Never: queued work beyond the in-memory bound is dropped and counted.

TimestampForm.description: Which points on a port carry a timestamp.

oneOf.description: Every point carries a timestamp.
No point carries a timestamp.
Points may or may not carry a timestamp.
